newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals end dull day narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals end dull day narrowly mixed.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based precious metal futures ended narrowly mixed on Monday with the benchmark back months barely weaker, while bullion prices were largely unchanged from their New York closing levels.
The foreign exchange market offered little direction to futures traders, with the yen only marginally weaker against the dollar from its New York close.

TOCOM most-active August 1997 gold settled one yen lower at 1,353 yen per gram, after edging upward to a fresh three-month high of 1,355 earlier in the session. The nearby months ended one weaker to two firmer.
Bullion closed at $381.20/50 an ounce, little changed from the New York close of $381.00/50.
TOCOM August 1997 platinum ended off three yen at 1,371 yen per gram, in line with weakness in overseas spot markets on Friday. The other months were four lower to one better.
Spot platinum settled at $385.25/$386.00, little changed from New York's closing quote of $385.30/$386.30 but down from Tokyo's Friday close of $387.50/$388.25.
Tokyo precious metal traders expected further near-term declines, after last week's rise to multi-week highs peaked on Thursday and the markets turned lower.
They predicted a test of $380 in gold and $382 in platinum.

Gold bullion trade was quiet in Asian hours today, with one trader noting that despite support from physical demand out of Hong Kong, Singapore and India, the threat of stepped-up Australian producer selling continued to weigh on the market.
In platinum, a build-up of speculative long positions in the TOCOM December futures and sluggish demand in Japan pointed to a weak market through the year's end, another trader said.
TOCOM August 1997 palladium ended two lower at 424 yen per gram. August silver was off 0.3 at 182.1 yen per 10 grams.
